results.title: PCB Tariffs from China to the US in 2026: HTS Codes, Section 301, and ...
results.content:
US PCB imports from China face HTS classification (8534 bare PCBs, 8473 PCBAs) and possible 25% Section 301 tariff. Landed cost = FOB + freight + duty + fees. Exclusions limited; de minimis not reliable in 2026. [...] PCB tariffs from China can significantly change the real cost of a U.S.-bound order before your boards reach production. A quote may look competitive at the factory level, but the final landed cost depends on the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) code, Section 301 duty, freight, customs fees, and exclusion status. For bare printed circuit boards (PCBs), classification typically starts with HTS 8534. For some PCB assemblies (PCBAs), HTS 8473.30 may apply, though classification depends on the [...] Section 301 tariffs apply in addition to the normal HTS duty rate. For many China-origin bare PCBs under HTS 8534.00 and certain PCBAs under HTS 8473.30.1180, the additional Section 301 tariff is 25% unless a product-specific exclusion applies.

Use this table as a planning reference only, not as a final classification decision. Verify current rates with your customs broker before placing any order.

results.title: PCB Import and Export Regulations: Tariffs, ITAR, Customs - PCBSync
results.content:
To import a printed circuit board into the United States you need four things right: the HTS classification, the country of origin, the duty stack that sits on top of the base rate, and, if the design touches defense work, an export-control answer before anyone sends a Gerber file overseas. Bare boards enter under HTS 8534.00 at a Most Favored Nation rate of Free, which fools a lot of first-time importers, because the base rate is not the bill. A China-origin board in August 2026 still carries [...] Going the other direction, into the EU, the duty picture is calmer than the U.S. picture. Printed circuits under heading 8534 generally carry a zero third-country duty rate, but import VAT of 19% to 27% depending on the member state applies to the customs value plus duty and freight, and it is recoverable only if you are properly registered. Budget the cash-flow effect even when the duty is nil.

## Common PCB Import and Export Mistakes That Cost Real Money [...] |  |  |  |
 --- 
| Regime | Who administers it | What it decides |
| Tariff classification and duty | CBP, using the HTSUS | Which 10-digit line your board falls under and what rate attaches |
| Country of origin | CBP, substantial transformation and marking rules | Which country’s tariff treatment applies, and what the label must say |
| Export control | State Department (ITAR/USML) and Commerce (EAR/CCL) | Whether you may send the board, or its design data, to a foreign person at all |
